prose: |
  docs/spec-hook-gates.tex models the SubagentStart verifier gate
  (checkVerifierHash, subagent_start.go:585-652) and the PreToolUse
  write gate (pretooluse.go:110-128) as one composed GateState
  machine. The MISSION_ID channel is an explicit free type,
  MissionIDChannel ::= midAbsent | midPresent<<MISSIONID>>, so
  absence is a distinct value rather than an empty string standing
  in for it; ETHOS_VERIFIER_ALLOWLIST is modelled as the write
  gate's sole input, abstracted behind a single boolean
  targetInAllowlist?, per the mission's own scoping instruction.

  The safety property -- a spawn that truly is the evaluator of an
  open mission (verifierOfOpenMission = ztrue, an exogenous ground
  truth frozen at Init and carried unchanged by every operation)
  ending up gated nowhere (gateApplied = zfalse) and diagnosed
  nowhere (diagnosticEmitted = zfalse) -- is deliberately kept out
  of GateState's own invariant, following spec-mission-lifecycle.tex
  section 6.2's errata technique exactly: baking it in would make
  MuteSkip's after-state unsatisfiable at exactly the states that
  exhibit the bug, producing a false-negative clean report instead
  of a genuine finding. Two decoupled scratch documents (not
  committed; .tmp/spec-hook-gates-mute.tex,
  .tmp/spec-hook-gates-loud.tex) retype the state as a minimal GateU
  with an Idle self-loop excluded exactly at the bad state, converting
  the safety property into a reachability question. Today's mute-skip
  semantics (subagent_start.go:599-605, modelled verbatim as MuteSkip)
  reaches the bad state in two steps and deadlocks there -- the
  recorded counter-example is INITIALISATION
  (verifierOfOpenMission := ztrue) then MuteSkip. A corrected loud-skip
  variant (identical gating decision, gateApplied' = zfalse; mandatory
  diagnostic, diagnosticEmitted' = ztrue unconditionally) explores the
  full 4-state space clean, matching bead ethos-yf6n's DO NOT FIX AS
  PROPOSED triage: the fix changes observability only.

  The three empty-MISSION_ID causes (Tier A ad-hoc spawn,
  PreToolUse mis-dispatch, PreToolUse not installed) are modelled as
  a free type, AbsenceCause, declared as an input to MuteSkip but
  never referenced in its predicate -- the CauseIndistinguishable
  theorem states, by that construction, that none of the three is
  distinguishable at this gate, under either the current or the
  corrected semantics: the channel is a single string, and presence
  or absence is the only bit it carries.

  The composition fact the mission asked to be recorded --
  ETHOS_VERIFIER_ALLOWLIST is set if and only if the SubagentStart
  gate applied -- is GateState's own invariant, allowlistActive =
  gateApplied (subagent_start.go:178-194's len(verifierMissions) > 0
  branch is the only place buildVerifierAllowlistEnv is called). The
  WritePassthroughWhenUngated theorem draws the corollary the mission
  brief singles out: whenever gateApplied = zfalse, WriteAllowedNoAllowlist
  is enabled for every Write/Edit with no further condition
  (pretooluse.go:110-113), so a MISSION_ID propagation failure
  disables the frozen-evaluator gate and write-set enforcement
  together, not separately.

  One real translation pitfall surfaced and is recorded in
  section "Tool run": probcli's Z-to-B translator rejects an Init
  schema that declares an input (identifier_not_found /
  initialisation_fails) -- an INITIALISATION operation has nothing to
  supply an input at machine start. Fixed by leaving
  verifierOfOpenMission' unconstrained at Init instead, matching how
  spec-mission-lifecycle.tex itself leaves evaluatorHash' and
  repoRootSet' unconstrained. Also recorded: probcli's constraint-based
  -cbc_deadlock check (used internally by the z-spec test/full-suite
  tool) finds the same bad valuation in both decoupled documents'
  raw state TYPE, because that check does not respect reachability
  from Init; the reachability-respecting -model_check is the correct
  oracle for this property and is what the verdicts above are drawn
  from -- this distinction is spelled out in the document itself so a
  future reader does not mistake -cbc_deadlock's "deadlock state
  found" on the loud variant for a regression.

  No Go files touched. make check passes (golangci-lint, shellcheck,
  ruff, mypy, pytest, markdownlint, go test -race ./..., validate-content,
  fuzz-check) with docs/spec-hook-gates.tex included in fuzz-check's
  docs/*.tex sweep.

Summary of the model: GateState composes the SubagentStart verifier gate (checkVerifierHash, subagent_start.go:585-652) and the PreToolUse write gate (pretooluse.go:110-128). MISSION_ID is an explicit free type, MissionIDChannel ::= midAbsent | midPresent<<MISSIONID>>, so absence is a real value, not empty-string-as-stand-in. ETHOS_VERIFIER_ALLOWLIST is the write gate's sole modelled input (path matching abstracted to one boolean, per the mission's own scoping).

Safety property kept out of GateState's own invariant, following spec-mission-lifecycle.tex section 6.2's errata technique verbatim (baking it in makes the buggy operation's after-state unsatisfiable — a false-negative clean report, not a real check). Two decoupled scratch documents (not committed: .tmp/spec-hook-gates-mute.tex, .tmp/spec-hook-gates-loud.tex) retype the state minimally with an Idle self-loop excluded at exactly the bad state. Today's mute-skip (subagent_start.go:599-605) reaches that state and deadlocks — counter-example: INITIALISATION(verifierOfOpenMission := ztrue), then MuteSkip, 3 states/7 transitions. The corrected loud-skip variant (same gating decision, mandatory diagnostic) explores its full 4-state/8-transition space clean — matches ethos-yf6n's DO NOT FIX AS PROPOSED triage exactly, since it changes diagnostics only.

The three empty-MISSION_ID causes (Tier A ad-hoc spawn, PreToolUse mis-dispatch, PreToolUse not installed) are modelled as a free type declared as MuteSkip's input but never referenced in its predicate — CauseIndistinguishable theorem: none of the three is distinguishable at this gate, by construction, under either semantics.

Composition fact recorded as GateState's own invariant: allowlistActive = gateApplied (subagent_start.go:178-194 is the only call site for buildVerifierAllowlistEnv). WritePassthroughWhenUngated theorem draws the corollary: when gateApplied = zfalse, every Write/Edit is allowed unconditionally (pretooluse.go:110-113) — the frozen-evaluator gate and write-set enforcement fail together, not separately.

One tooling gotcha worth flagging to the other Z-spec workers: probcli's Z-to-B translator rejects an Init schema that takes an explicit input (identifier_not_found/initialisation_fails) — leave the primed variable unconstrained instead, exactly as spec-mission-lifecycle.tex already does for evaluatorHash'/repoRootSet'. Also: probcli's -cbc_deadlock is constraint-based and does NOT respect reachability from Init, so it flags a "deadlock" in both mute and loud variants' raw state type even though the loud variant is unreachable-clean under exhaustive -model_check — model_check is the correct oracle for a reachability safety property, documented explicitly in the spec so nobody mistakes cbc_deadlock's report for a regression later.
